headline: Nvidia's beat lifts KOSPI back above 5,000 and the KDI raises 2027 growth to 3.9%: the KTB 3Y rises 1.1bp to 3.736% and the 10Y 0.9bp to 3.975%, against a 0.9bp fall implied by the overnight Treasury rally, so the whole move was local
summary: KTBs traded with the stock market all day: firmer into midday as KOSPI gave up an early 3% jump, then weaker as institutions pushed it back up 1.99% to 5,067. The 3Y closed 1.1bp higher at 3.736% (56th percentile of its 1-year range), the 10Y 0.9bp higher at 3.975% (51st) and the 30Y 0.5bp higher at 4.060%, with the 5Y (+1.4bp) leading, so the 3s5s10s fly rose 0.8bp and 10s30s flattened 0.4bp to 8.5bp; the 50Y was unchanged. The 1Y is 3.635% (90th) and bills sit at 1-year highs (MSB 91-day 3.209%, CP 3.84%; CD eased 1bp to 3.37%), so a November 26 hike stays fully priced. Spread products barely moved: AAA bank 1Y is 36.0bp over KTB (71st, 1.4bp tighter), AA- 3Y 67.3bp (66th) and KEPCO 3Y 40.8bp (79th); the KDB 3Y fit, re-run on 28 trades, now reads 24.9bp over (79th), well above the 12bp we showed yesterday.
drivers: Nvidia beat on revenue (USD 115.8bn vs about 109bn expected) and guided to USD 130bn, so KOSPI opened 2.6% higher, slipped to 4,943 by midday as foreigners turned sellers, and closed +1.99% at 5,067 on KRW 512bn of institutional buying (foreigners −327bn, a fourth day of selling). The 3Y was 0.3bp lower at 3.722% in the morning and finished 1.1bp higher, a 1.4bp swing that tracked the index.
Growth upgrades keep the hike path open

A day after the IMF, the KDI raised 2026 growth to 3.8% (from 3.2%) and 2027 to 3.9% (from 2.2%), with about two-thirds of next year's growth from chips. That backs a Nov 26 hike and puts the focus on the BOK's new dot plot and forecasts; the 5Y led the sell-off (+1.4bp) and the MSB 2Y rose 1.5bp to 3.760%.
Treasuries explain none of today's move

The US 10Y fell 2bp to 5.10% on Nov 17 as stocks slid and retail sales came in line (+0.2%), despite St. Louis Fed President Musalem talking of several more hikes. At the 1-year beta of 0.47 that implied −0.9bp for the KTB 10Y; it rose 0.9bp, so the 1.8bp gap was all local. The KTB–UST 10Y gap is −112.5bp, still the widest of the past year (0th percentile).

Foreigners bought 316 3Y and 1,670 10Y futures after selling 3,140 10Y on Tuesday. Our basket fair values fell 5 ticks to 103.59 (3Y) and 9 ticks to 108.38 (10Y); the KRX settles were not in the wraps we read, so we leave the basis at Tuesday's read (3Y about 10 ticks cheap, 10Y about 2 rich). USD/KRW fell 5.2 won to 1,333.0, and Q3 household credit grew only KRW 9.8tn, the smallest rise in six quarters.
data: In line; US 10Y −2bp on the day.
view: Today was a local day: Treasuries implied −0.9bp for the 10Y and it rose 0.9bp, so +1.8bp came from the KOSPI rebound and the KDI upgrade; over four weeks the 10Y's −12.2bp splits into +8.8bp from Treasuries (weekly beta 0.63, US 10Y +14bp) and −21.0bp of Korea's own rally.

The rotation signal still reads bond rally (weekly +1.10, daily +1.33) but it is fading from +1.62 four weeks ago, because KOSPI is back above 5,000 although still 8.7% lower over four weeks, and margin credit is down 12.7%.

With a hike priced and official forecasts moving to 3.8–3.9% growth, I expect the 10Y to hold 3.90–4.05% into the BOK and the curve to stay flat (3s10s 23.9bp, 2nd percentile), so I stay out of steepeners.

Book: keep the 10Y long (average 3.975%, flat outright, about +3bp hedged), take profit on the 30Y-into-50Y switch at target (+5.6bp), and start a KDB 3Y overweight now that the spread is back above 20bp.

Hedging the rotation view against Treasuries remains the better way to hold it: weekly hedged rally calls were right 68% of the time and sell-off calls 69% (Sharpe 1.33, worst drawdown −26bp) against 52%, 57%, 0.91 and −36bp outright; FOMC minutes tonight and the BOK's dot plot on Nov 26 are the main risks.

buckets.name: KTB 1–2Y front end
buckets.why: The 2Y rose 0.8bp to 3.735%, 83rd percentile of its 1-year range (average 3.40%), and the 1Y is 3.635% (90th). 2s3s is 0.1bp (2nd percentile, average 13bp) and 1s2s 10.0bp (4th). MSB 91-day (3.209%) and CP (3.84%) are at 1-year highs and price a hike to 3.25% on Nov 26; Citi and Bloomberg Economics see 3.5% by the first quarter.
buckets.call: Keep: buy the 2Y above 3.80%, target 3.65%, stop 3.90%. Not triggered (6.5bp away).

buckets.name: 3s10s curve
buckets.why: 3s10s flattened 0.2bp to 23.9bp (2nd percentile, average 39.5bp, 1-year low 20.8bp). The 3s5s10s fly rose 0.8bp to −3.3bp (14th, average 4.3bp) as the 5Y led today's sell-off, so the belly keeps cheapening from very rich levels. Our earlier steepener was stopped on Nov 5.
buckets.call: Stay flat: KOSPI closed at 5,067, below the 5,300 re-entry trigger. Re-enter the steepener (3 × 3Y vs 1 × 10Y futures, DV01 about KRW 86k each side) only on a KOSPI close above 5,300 or after a BOK hike; target 32bp, stop 19bp.

buckets.name: KTB 10Y outright
buckets.why: The 10Y at 3.975% sits at the 51st percentile of a 3.25–4.60% range (average 3.92%). Treasuries implied −0.9bp and the 10Y rose 0.9bp, so the hedged long gave back about 2bp today. The new 10Y (26-13) still trades about 6.5bp rich to the fitted curve, the richest liquid line.
buckets.call: Long, average 3.975%, stop 4.10%, target 3.85%; hold against about 0.5 × US 10Y. Open, flat outright, about +3bp hedged.

buckets.name: Ultra-long 30–50Y
buckets.why: 30s50s fell 0.5bp to −3.1bp as the 50Y held while the 30Y rose 0.5bp, so the 30Y-into-50Y switch from +2.5bp hit its −3bp target (+5.6bp). The spread is still at the 84th percentile (average −9.0bp), so the 50Y stays cheap against history. The 10s20s30s fly fell 0.8bp to 13.7bp (77th).
buckets.call: Closed at target, +5.6bp. Re-enter the 30Y-into-50Y switch on a back-up to 0bp; target −5bp, stop +2.5bp.

buckets.name: KDB 1–3Y vs KTB
buckets.why: With 28 trades the KDB fit now puts the 3Y 24.9bp over KTB, 79th percentile (average 19.6bp); the Nov 17 point was re-fitted to 24.3bp from the 12.3bp we used yesterday, so this is a data revision more than a sell-off. The 1Y fit is 25.6bp over (45th) and KOFIA's 1Y quote 24.3bp (46th). IBK is 28.4bp over on a flat 10-trade fit and KEXIM 33.7bp on 8 trades, also flat (low confidence).
buckets.call: New: our re-entry level (above 20bp) is met, so overweight KDB 3Y vs KTB 3Y at 24.9bp; target 18bp, stop 30bp. Half size until the fit holds for a few sessions.

buckets.name: AAA bank debentures and money market
buckets.why: AAA bank paper (42-trade fit) is 36.0bp over the 1Y KTB, 71st percentile (average 30.9bp), 1.4bp tighter on the day; the 3Y is 28.8bp over (50th). CD eased 1bp to 3.37% while CP held at 3.84%, so CP–CD widened to 47bp (91st, average 29bp) and CD–MSB91 is 16bp (25th).
buckets.call: No change: revisit bank paper once CP–CD falls below 35bp; prefer the 1Y over the 3Y if adding.

buckets.name: Corporate credit (AA- 3Y)
buckets.why: AA- 3Y rose 0.7bp to 4.409%, less than the KTB 3Y, so the spread tightened 0.4bp to 67.3bp (66th percentile, average 61.7bp). KEPCO 3Y is 40.8bp over (79th, average 34.8bp) and BBB- minus AA- 583bp (74th). Credit is holding up despite the equity swings.
buckets.call: Add AA- only above 75bp or once KOSPI regains 5,300; no trigger hit.

watch: Next: FOMC minutes (Nov 18 US time), the college entrance exam on Nov 19 (KRX opens an hour late), the APEC summit in Shenzhen (Nov 19–20), Nov 1–20 exports around Nov 23, the BOK decision, dot plot and new forecasts on Nov 26 (hike to 3.25% priced) and the FOMC on Dec 8–9; KTBs take about 0.45–0.5bp per Treasury bp on the day.
